newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up for fifth day in a row.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up for fifth day in a row.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index rose 0.7 percent on Tuesday, taking total gains over the past five days to 5.2 percent.
Traders said stong international buying was expected to push the index up to 1,500 points by the end of the week.
"I believe international investors currently account for about 60 percent of the volume on the main market," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst at bank A banka.
* The SBI index rose 10.28 points to 1,469.85.
* Issue A of drug company Lek was most actively traded, up 2.65 percent to 34,900 tolars on volume of 11,543 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
